title: To Thy Temple I Repair
description: To Thy Temple I Repair in Tonic Solfa to INNOCENTS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 5 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 8.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to INNOCENTS; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: To Thy tem-ple I re-pair; Lord, I love to wor-ship there. While Thy glo-rious praise is sung, Touch my lips, un-loose my tongue.

lines: To Thy temple I repair;
Lord, I love to worship there.
While Thy glorious praise is sung,
Touch my lips, unloose my tongue.
While the prayers of saints ascend,
God of Love, to mine attend.
Hear me, for Thy Spirit pleads;
Hear, for Jesus intercedes.
While I hearken to Thy Law,
Fill my soul with humble awe,
Till Thy Gospel bring to me
Life and immortality.
While Thy ministers proclaim
Peace and pardon in Thy name,
Through their voice, by faith, may I
Hear Thee speaking from the sky.
From Thy house, when I return,
May my heart within me burn;
And at evening let me say,
“I have walked with God to-day.”

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to INNOCENTS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
